key_decisions: ref2va got its OWN op rather than riding t2v_ms. mediaInputs live on the OP, so 15 slots would land in front of LTX and WAN behind 15 capability gates; t2v_ms already declares an audio slot titled `Input_audio` where this graph has `Input_Audio`, which injection would SILENTLY skip; and references are not a first frame, so 'Image to Video' would be an actively wrong label.

capabilities.audio is TRUE on ref2va and FALSE on fl2va, and it is load-bearing: filterMediaInputsForModel hard-drops every audio slot from a model that does not declare it, so without it the three audio reference wells vanish. negativePrompt:false is what keeps that honest — capabilities.audio also arms the MPI-474 audio-negative stop, and this graph has neither an Input_Negative_Audio nor an Input_Negative node. Every capabilities.audio consumer was swept.

THE AUDIO ORDINAL PROBLEM AND ITS FIX. Core shares ONE audio sequence between reference videos and standalone clips, emitting a video's soundtrack BEFORE its <Video k>, so a sounded reference video pushes the first standalone clip to <Audio 2>. Whether a video HAS a soundtrack is a property of the FILE (MpiLoadVideo returns a 1-sample sentinel for a track-less one and collect_refs drops it), so the ordinal moves on a fact nobody knows until decode time. Neither the app nor the user can label the wells up front. Fix: the NODE translates, at execution, where both numberings are known. REJECTED the alternative of always emitting the soundtrack slot — _encode_ref_audio resamples then VAE-encodes, and a 1-sample tensor at movedim(1,-1) is a crash or a degenerate latent.
Chips are SLOT-numbered and must stay that way. Do not add app-side hasAudio probing; the node owns the translation.

KJNodes H3 patches rejected on measurement, not taste: they save VRAM neither target card is short of. The 16GB baseline completed without them (offload-bound, 24GB in shared, RAM at 95%, GPU at 97%), and on a 5090 — the expected primary card — the encoder unloads before sampling so the ~21GB transformer is resident in 32GB with nothing to save. Both patches ARE mathematically exact; the outputs matched, as predicted.
